beats.label: S1 · Shift change
beats.text: Attending Robby starts a shift with new residents Santos and Mel, and students Whitaker and Javadi, relieving overnight attending Abbot.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the ensemble the reader must recognise before anything else lands.

beats.label: S1 · Adamson under the surface
beats.text: As pressure mounts, Robby has flashbacks to the COVID pandemic and the death of his mentor Adamson in the Pitt, a loss he has never processed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Robby's unresolved grief is the fuse that eventually ignites his S2 sabbatical.

beats.label: S1 · Langdon exposed
beats.text: Santos suspects senior resident Langdon of stealing patient sedatives; Robby confirms it, finds stolen doses in his locker, and sends him home in disgrace.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the exact wound S2 opens on when Langdon returns from rehab.

beats.label: S1 · Collins miscarries
beats.text: Senior resident Collins, secretly early in pregnancy, miscarries in the bathroom mid-shift and immediately returns to work, telling only Dana.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Collins's private grief becomes the hidden weight she carries into the aftermath.

beats.label: S1 · Pitt Fest shooting
beats.text: A mass shooting at Pitt Fest overwhelms the ER; the hospital activates its mass casualty protocols as wave after wave of victims arrive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The event that shatters everyone and reshapes the emotional baseline going into S2.

beats.label: S1 · Leah dies, Robby breaks
beats.text: Jake, the son of Robby's ex, arrives with girlfriend Leah, who dies despite Robby's efforts; Robby collapses in a panic attack over Leah and Adamson.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The specific loss that pushes Robby's suicidal ideation over the edge — the origin of the S2 sabbatical.

beats.label: S1 · Shift ends bloodied
beats.text: McKay is arrested for smashing her ankle monitor, Dana tells Robby she may quit, and Abbot finds Robby on the roof and talks him back down.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The closing state of the staff — every thread the reader must carry into S2's opening.

cliffhanger.text: Robby is off the roof but hollow. The shift ended with Langdon sent home for theft, McKay arrested, Dana ready to quit, and the ER staggering out of a mass shooting that killed Jake's girlfriend Leah.
questions: Will Robby come back to work, or step away for good?
Can Langdon salvage his career and his sobriety after being exposed?
Will Dana actually quit after Doug's assault?

characters.name: Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch
characters.line: Day-shift attending; a 15-hour shift ending in a mass shooting has cracked open unresolved COVID-era grief, and Abbot has just talked him off the roof.

characters.name: Dr. Jack Abbot
characters.line: Overnight attending and Robby's counterpart; wears a prosthetic leg from military service, and stayed to help when the shooting hit.

characters.name: Dr. Frank Langdon
characters.line: Senior resident exposed as an opioid thief; sent home by Robby, his career and sobriety in question.

characters.name: Dr. Trinity Santos
characters.line: Brash, first-year resident who blew the whistle on Langdon; competent but constantly clashing with colleagues.

characters.name: Dr. Mel King
characters.line: Quiet first-year resident who grew into a confident doctor over the shift, and picks up her autistic sister Becca as it ends.

characters.name: Dr. Cassie McKay
characters.line: Resident wearing a court-ordered ankle monitor; disabled it to work through the shooting, and was arrested for it as the shift closed.

characters.name: Dr. Heather Collins
characters.line: Senior resident who lost her early pregnancy in a bathroom mid-shift and returned to work without telling most of the team.

characters.name: Dr. Samira Mohan
characters.line: Resident whose patient-first pace Robby criticised, then defended; cried in the bathroom as the adrenaline wore off.

characters.name: Dana Evans
characters.line: Charge nurse punched by an angry patient in the ambulance bay; kept working, but told Robby she may not come back.

characters.name: Dennis Whitaker
characters.line: Fourth-year medical student secretly squatting in a hospital room; Santos invited him to move into her apartment.

beats.label: S2 · Last shift before sabbatical
beats.text: On July 4, Robby begins his last shift before a planned three-month sabbatical, handing the department to interim attending Al-Hashimi as Langdon returns from rehab.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets every major running thread: Robby's exit, Al-Hashimi in charge, Langdon's return.

beats.label: S2 · Langdon on triage, Santos unmoved
beats.text: Robby keeps Langdon on triage and withholds trust; Santos rejects Langdon's apology and demands he publicly admit to stealing hospital drugs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The unresolved S1 exposure now defines Langdon's slow, incomplete rehabilitation.

beats.label: S2 · Ransomware shuts the ER down
beats.text: A regional ransomware attack takes the hospital's computers offline mid-shift, forcing the staff onto paper charts and a hand-updated whiteboard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Operational spine of the middle stretch — every subsequent case runs under this handicap.

beats.label: S2 · Waterslide mass casualty
beats.text: A nearby waterslide collapse sends a mass-casualty wave into an already-strained ER; Al-Hashimi saves a child with an emergency slash tracheotomy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Second MCI in two seasons — the specific event that starts breaking Al-Hashimi's composure.

beats.label: S2 · ICE seizes a patient
beats.text: ICE agents seize an injured detainee from the ER, arresting nurse Jesse when he tries to intervene and sending other patients fleeing in terror.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jesse's arrest and the fallout for undocumented patients is a thread left open at shift's end.

beats.label: S2 · Duke's aneurysm, Santos's scalpels
beats.text: Robby's friend Duke arrives with an aortic aneurysm; Dana and McKay warn Robby his sabbatical looks suicidal, while Santos quietly pockets scalpel kits.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment Robby's suicidal plan becomes explicit — and Santos's self-harm risk surfaces.

beats.label: S2 · Seizures, a baby, a safer trip
beats.text: Al-Hashimi confesses her seizures have returned and is pulled off shift; Robby cradles an abandoned baby and accepts Abbot's advice to take a safer trip.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Robby's arc without resolving it and pulls Al-Hashimi out of the driver's seat.

cliffhanger.text: Robby is finally leaving, but on a safer trip after Abbot pulled him back from the edge. Santos is hiding scalpel kits, Dana may lose her license, Langdon is only halfway rehabilitated, and Al-Hashimi has been forced off shift by returning seizures.
questions: How far will Santos's self-harm spiral go?
Will Dana keep her nursing license after the off-protocol Versed?
Can Al-Hashimi return to practice, and who runs the ER if she cannot?

characters.name: Dr. Michael "Robby" Robinavitch
characters.line: Day attending finally taking his delayed sabbatical on a safer trip; his suicidal ideation was named but is not resolved.

characters.name: Dr. Jack Abbot
characters.line: Night attending and SWAT medic; talked Robby down a second time, urging him to accept help.

characters.name: Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi
characters.line: Interim senior attending whose seizure disorder returned mid-shift; pulled off duty pending disclosure and treatment.

characters.name: Dr. Frank Langdon
characters.line: Senior resident back from rehab; kept on triage, cold-shouldered by Santos and Al-Hashimi, slowly rebuilding after saving a spinal case.

characters.name: Dr. Trinity Santos
characters.line: Second-year resident increasingly isolated and abrasive; pocketed scalpel kits at shift's end, a possible relapse into self-harm.

characters.name: Dr. Mel King
characters.line: Resident whose malpractice deposition over the Flynn spinal tap went well; grappling with her sister Becca's growing independence.

characters.name: Dr. Cassie McKay
characters.line: Resident continuing her sobriety alongside Langdon; lost her patient Roxie to cancer and warned Robby he seems to be courting death.

characters.name: Dr. Samira Mohan
characters.line: Resident shattered by patient Orlando's condition, which Robby speculated was a suicide attempt; unsure about her future.

characters.name: Dana Evans
characters.line: Charge nurse still on duty; subdued a violent patient with off-protocol Versed, putting her nursing license at risk.

characters.name: Dennis Whitaker
characters.line: Fourth-year medical student housesitting for Robby during the sabbatical; left with Amy Miller as the shift ended.
